audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may treat trapped or taxable foreign cash as fully distributable
audit_findings.magnitude: $299.9 million of the $370.5 million cash balance was held by foreign subsidiaries; the required haircut is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all cash to common-equity value without deducting repatriation taxes, restricted cash, or minimum operating cash.
audit_findings.evidence: Should we make a determination to remit the cash and cash equivalents from our foreign subsidiaries that are considered indefinitely reinvested to Herbalife Ltd. for the purpose of repatriation of undistributed earnings, we would need to accrue and pay taxes.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved valuation possibility, not a demonstrated error: the filing confirms potential repatriation taxes and currency restrictions but does not identify the affected cash or tax cost. The $299.9 million foreign-cash pool equals $2.16 per diluted valuation share and 13.6% of base equity value, so even a partial haircut could materially alter scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June 2026 cash by jurisdiction and legal owner; identify indefinitely reinvested earnings, restricted balances, currency controls, and minimum operating cash; calculate applicable withholding and repatriation taxes; then rerun the bridge with distributable net cash only.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter misses an outside claim on Pro2col
audit_findings.magnitude: 10% current outside ownership; $7.5 million paid for the additional 5%; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated OE and its growth must exclude the noncontrolling owner's share of Pro2col, or the resulting outside claim must be deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Subsequently, during February 2026, Ronaldo’s equity‑holding entity exercised an option and purchased an additional 5 % equity interest in Pro2col Software for $ 7.5 million, increasing its ownership to 10 % on a fully diluted basis.
audit_findings.explanation: The outside ownership is demonstrated, but a material valuation error is not established because Pro2col-specific OE, projected cash flows, and the allocation of the reported $7.6 million total noncontrolling interest are unavailable. The remaining options could raise outside ownership by another 10%, but that is prospective.
audit_findings.action: Produce Pro2col standalone historical and scenario cash flows, reconcile the June 2026 noncontrolling-interest balance by subsidiary, allocate 10% of Pro2col economics to the current outside owner, and separately model dilution from the remaining options through January 2028.

audit_findings.title: Subscriber growth can trigger acquisition payments not captured in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $46 million nominal through 2035, equal to at most $0.33 per valuation share before probability weighting and discounting
audit_findings.mechanism: Subscriber-driven contingent acquisition payments are future cash outflows that should reduce projected OE or be deducted from the equity bridge when the triggering growth is assumed.
audit_findings.evidence: Third, there are multiple milestone contingent payments ranging from $ 5 million to $ 15 million each, with the aggregate amount of these contingent payments not to exceed $ 46 million in total, that are contingent upon the Company achieving specific monthly active subscriber milestones; these contingent payments will be made if and when Pro2col monthly active subscriber milestones are achieved during the 10-year period which expires in 2035, and if the minimum targets for the monthly active subscriber milestones are not reached, then no additional payments will be required under these respective contingencies.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual obligation is demonstrated, but payment depends on future subscriber milestones and no scenario-level probability or timing is supplied. The undiscounted maximum is 2.1% of base equity value and does not by itself overturn the base value or margin-of-safety threshold, although it nearly equals the $0.35 per-share cushion between bear value and market price.
audit_findings.action: Map each valuation scenario to Pro2col monthly-active-subscriber milestones, assign payment timing and probabilities, discount the expected payments, and rerun any scenario that assumes the associated subscriber growth.

audit_findings.title: Material tax assessments remain outside the recognized liability base
audit_findings.magnitude: $99.2 million of filed Indian income-tax assessments, or approximately $0.72 per valuation share and 4.5% of base equity value; additional interest, penalties, and later-year exposure are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An adverse settlement would create cash outflows ahead of common shareholders that are absent from recurring OE and from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, the Indian income tax authorities audited the Company’s fiscal years ended March 31, 2017, 2018, 2020, 2021, and 2022 and the Company has received assessments for tax and interest of approximately $ 16.2 million, $ 15.7 million, $ 20.6 million, $ 18.2 million, and $ 33.7 million for those respective years, translated at the December 31, 2025 spot rate.
audit_findings.explanation: The assessments and absence of an accrual are demonstrated, but a valuation overstatement is not yet demonstrated because Herbalife expects to prevail and favorable decisions exist for two years. The $99.2 million disclosed amount exceeds the approximately $48.5 million equity-value cushion between the bear value and market price, so a sufficiently adverse probability-weighted outcome could change the downside conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each assessment to the $43.5 million reported unrecognized-tax-benefit balance and all existing reserves, obtain case-specific probability and timing estimates including interest and penalties, incorporate Brazil and Mexico without double counting collateral, and rerun OE or the bridge using the probability-weighted net exposure.

audit_findings.title: The convertible-note share ceiling does not match the contractual settlement claim
audit_findings.magnitude: 16.344695 million shares, 11.8% of the 138.641075 million-share denominator; removing that full block at the fixed $2.212 billion base equity value would increase value from $15.96 to approximately $18.09 per share before applying correct conversion-spread dilution
audit_findings.mechanism: The denominator includes the full principal-equivalent conversion shares even though principal must be paid in cash and only the conversion spread may be share-settled.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon conversion, the principal portion of the 2028 Convertible Notes will be settled in cash and to the extent the conversion value exceeds the principal amount, the Company may elect to settle in cash, or a combination of cash and common shares, based on the applicable conversion rate at such time.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated denominator-method error. The contractual settlement terms and the filing's diluted-EPS method both limit potential share dilution to the conversion spread. The illustrative $2.13-per-share base impact is large enough to change the valuation conclusion, although the final correction must reflect share-price-dependent spread dilution, conversion-rate adjustments, and the cash principal claim consistently.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate the denominator under the contractual conversion-spread method for each scenario, including the current conversion price and adjustments; treat the $277.5 million cash-settled principal consistently with the equity-level OE method; then rerun all per-share values and the buy-below threshold.

audit_findings.title: Digital spending is explicitly ongoing and may be understated as maintenance reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 capital expenditures were $80.4 million; 2026 guidance is $50 million to $70 million of capital expenditures plus $35 million to $55 million of capitalizable SaaS implementation costs; any OE misstatement is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring platform replacement, enhancement, cybersecurity, member-tool, and SaaS implementation cash costs reduce sustainable OE through maintenance reinvestment or operating cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: As we plan to continue investing broadly in digital technology and infrastructure, these costs will be part of our ongoing capital expenditures and future spending.
audit_findings.explanation: Ongoing digital spending is demonstrated, but the record does not show how the $138.6 million OE anchor classified these costs. SaaS implementation cash costs may already reduce operating cash flow, while capital expenditures may already be included in the OE calculation, so double counting must be avoided. Without the OE workpaper and a maintenance-versus-growth allocation, materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every 2025 and projected 2026 digital cash outflow to operating cash flow, capital expenditures, and the OE calculation; classify recurring maintenance separately from incremental growth investment; document asset lives and replacement cycles; then rerun the anchor and scenarios for any omitted recurring amount.
